leaf.text:
Intel TDX (Trust Domain Extensions) provides a new kind of virtual machine guest called a Trust Domain (TD). A TD runs in a CPU mode that is designed to protect the confidentiality of its memory contents and its CPU state from other software, including the host's hypervisor itself — unless explicitly shared by the TD.
This leaf is available if cpuid leaf 0x1 @guest_status is set and cpuid leaf 0x0 @max_std_leaf ≥ 0x21.
Reference: Architecture Specification: Intel Trust Domain Extensions (Intel TDX) Module, February 2023. Section 13.2., "Guest TD Run Time Environment Enumeration."

subleaf.text: If the returned vendor ID string is "IntelTDX ", then the guest is running as a Trust Domain (i.e., not a "legacy virtual machine" guest) and guest-side TDCALL(TDG.VP.INFO) can be used to enumerate the TD execution environment.

bit0.text: Equals "Inte" if the guest is running as a TD.
Equals " " if the guest is running as a TD.
Equals "lTDX" if the guest is running as a TD.
